description:
BIG-IP Advanced WAF and BIG-IP ASM systems incorrectly handle certain requests.

This issue occurs when the following condition is met:

BIG-IP Advanced WAF and BIG-IP ASM handle a malicious request when a parameter with Base64 decoding is enabled.
impact:
The attack signature check fails to detect and block such requests.

Symptoms

As a result of this issue, you may encounter the following symptom:

The back-end server receives requests that should have been blocked by the Advanced WAF and BIG-IP ASM systems.
mitigation:
To mitigate this issue, you can enable blocking for the Illegal Base64 value violation in the affected security policies. To do so, perform the following procedure:

Impact of action: Enabling the Illegal Base64 value violation will cause the policy to strictly block requests containing base64 values for which the system cannot cleanly decode (including those values found in HTTP headers and parameters1). This may cause an increase in false positive violations if the web application is expected to handle malformed base64 values.

Enable blocking for the Illegal Base64 value violation

Log in to the Configuration utility.
Go to Security > Application Security > Policy Building > Learning and Blocking Settings.
Select the name of the policy you want to edit from the list.
Select Advanced to display the advanced Policy Builder settings (13.x - 14.x only).
Select General Settings.
For the Illegal Base64 value violation, select Block.

Note: For generic security policy templates, blocking is enabled by default for the Illegal Base64 value violation.

Select Save.
Select Apply Policy.

1Note that this security exposure only applies to Parameter values. It does not apply to encoded Header values, however the “Illegal Base64 value” violation applies to both.
recommended_actions:
If you are running a version listed in the Versions affected by this issue column, you can eliminate this issue by installing a version listed in the Fixes introduced in column. If the Fixes introduced in column does not list a version for your branch, then no update candidate currently exists for that branch and F5 recommends upgrading to a version with the fix (refer to the table).

If the Fixes introduced in column lists a version prior to the one you are running, in the same branch, then your version should have the fix.

F5 Product Development has assigned ID 1069501 (BIG-IP) to this issue. This issue has been classified as CWE-20: Improper Input Validation.

To determine if your product and version have been evaluated for this issue, refer to the Applies to (see versions) box.
